Specification: Standard TLAPS prover-pragma module: defines named backend pragmas (Z3, SMT, Zenon, Isabelle, CVC3, veriT, Yices, SPASS, LS4/PTL, multi-prover combinators) and the TLA proof rules (TLA1, TLA2, INV1, INV2, WF1/WF2, SF1/SF2, InvImplication, StepSimulation) used by TLAPS proofs.
AssumeProveBlocks: ASSUME STATE P, STATE f, P /\ (f' = f) => P' PROVE []P <=> P /\ [][P => P']_f
ASSUME STATE P, STATE Q, STATE f, STATE g, ACTION A, ACTION B, P /\ [A]_f => Q /\ [B]_g PROVE []P /\ [][A]_f => []Q /\ [][B]_g
ASSUME STATE I, STATE F, ACTION N, I /\ [N]_F => I' PROVE I /\ [][N]_F => []I
ASSUME STATE I, STATE f, ACTION N PROVE []I => ([][N]_f <=> [][N /\ I /\ I']_f)
ASSUME STATE P, STATE Q, STATE f, ACTION N, ACTION A, P /\ [N]_f => (P' \/ Q'), P /\ <<N /\ A>>_f => Q', P => ENABLED <<A>>_f PROVE [][N]_f /\ WF_f(A) => (P ~> Q)

ASSUME STATE P, STATE Q, STATE f, ACTION N, ACTION A, TEMPORAL F, P /\ [N]_f => (P' \/ Q'), P /\ <<N /\ A>>_f => Q', []P /\ [][N]_f /\ []F => <> ENABLED <<A>>_f PROVE [][N]_f /\ SF_f(A) /\ []F => (P ~> Q)

ASSUME STATE P, STATE f, STATE g, STATE EM, ACTION A, ACTION B, ACTION N, ACTION M, TEMPORAL F, <<N /\ B>>_f => <<M>>_g, P /\ P' /\ <<N /\ A>>_f /\ EM => B, P /\ EM => ENABLED A, [][N /\ ~B]_f /\ WF_f(A) /\ []F /\ <>[]EM => <>[]P PROVE [][N]_f /\ WF_f(A) /\ []F => []<><<M>>_g \/ []<>(~EM)

ASSUME STATE P, STATE f, STATE g, STATE EM, ACTION A, ACTION B, ACTION N, ACTION M, TEMPORAL F, <<N /\ B>>_f => <<M>>_g, P /\ P' /\ <<N /\ A>>_f /\ EM => B, P /\ EM => ENABLED A, [][N /\ ~B]_f /\ SF_f(A) /\ []F /\ []<>EM => <>[]P PROVE [][N]_f /\ SF_f(A) /\ []F => []<><<M>>_g \/ <>[](~EM)
ASSUME STATE F, STATE G, F => G PROVE []F => []G
ASSUME STATE I, STATE f, STATE g, ACTION M, ACTION N, I /\ I' /\ [M]_f => [N]_g PROVE []I /\ [][M]_f => [][N]_g
DivisionNotes: Every operator in OperatorDefNames is defined as the Boolean constant TRUE (used as a backend pragma) and contains no primes or temporal operators; classified as StatePredicate.
TemporalNesting is true because the proof-rule theorems contain nested temporal operators such as []<>EM and <>[]P (RuleWF2, RuleSF2).
